entries.title: Glamorgan Artillery Barracks, Penarth; Volunteer Rifle Corps and Severn Sub-marine Miners
entries.quote: The Glamorgan Artillery Barracks and Quarters were opened in the 1860s ... By 1892 the official address had changed to 32 High Street. ... The Quarters were used by various military groups - not only the Artillery, but also the Penarth Volunteer Rifle Corps and the Severn Sub-marine Miners.
entries.source: Alan Thorne, Place Names of Penarth (D. Brown & Sons, 1997), pp.13-14
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Penarth town, about 2 km from Tŷ Mawr (Great House); no link to the farm.
entries.next: Glamorgan Archives catalogue enquiry (free) for 2nd Glamorgan Volunteer Artillery records.

entries.title: War Office land record for Lavernock Point
entries.quote: Lavernock Point
entries.source: TNA LRRO 1/3531 (Land Revenue Record Office), catalogue entry
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Catalogue title only; that it is a War Office acquisition is not checked. Lavernock parish, not Llandough.
entries.next: Read LRRO 1/3531 at Kew (free reader's ticket) or ask TNA's free 'Ask us' service what the file covers.

entries.title: Royal Artillery Establishment at Lavernock (plans 1879, corrected to May 1899)

entries.source: TNA WO 78/2281, catalogue description
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Shows a War Office establishment at Lavernock, the trial site; nothing about Llandough or Tŷ Mawr (Great House).
entries.next: View WO 78/2281 at Kew (free); the May 1899 sheet shows the battery's extent two years after the trials.

entries.title: Preece's induction signals, Lavernock to Flat Holm
entries.quote: (Preece's own account, South Wales Daily Post 5 Jun 1897 p.3; Cardiff Times 13 Mar 1897 p.2)
entries.source: Welsh Newspapers Online

entries.cuts: A Post Office trial, not a military one.

entries.title: 2nd Glamorgan Volunteer Artillery 64-pounder competition at Lavernock
entries.quote: The 64-pounder group competition of the 2nd G.V.A. was continued at Lavernock on Saturday last in the presence of Colonel H. U. Fisher.
entries.source: Barry Dock News, 22 Jan 1897, p.5
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: Routine volunteer gunnery practice; no link to Marconi or the farm.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Military funeral at Penarth of a gunner of the Lavernock battery
entries.quote: The remains of Chas. Gowing, pensioner, of the Woolwich Royal Horse Artillery, and latterly stationed at the local battery at Lavernock ... were interred at St. Augustine's Church on Saturday with full military honours.
entries.source: South Wales Echo, 19 Jan 1897, p.3
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: Shows a staffed battery at Lavernock four months before the trials; nothing more.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Annual group firing competition opens at Lavernock
entries.quote: On Saturday last the annual group firing competition for members of the 2nd Glamorgan Volunteer Artillery opened at Lavernock. Colonel Fisher was present, and the range officer was Major Rigg. The following companies took part:—No. 3 (Cardiff), No. 5 (Cardiff), No. 9 (Penarth), No. 10 (Penarth)
entries.source: Evening Express, 25 Mar 1897, p.1
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: Volunteer training at an existing battery, about six weeks before Marconi arrived; no link to the farm.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Marconi's stay at Tŷ Mawr (Great House)
entries.quote: (Glamorgan Village Book, 1993; The Post, 14 Sep 1995, p.24)
entries.source: published accounts held on the site
entries.label: testimony
entries.cuts: No 1897 document names Marconi's lodging (Fahie, Kemp's diary, 77 Welsh press hits for 1897 searched). Kemp's diary names Penarth for the apparatus only.
entries.next: IET Archives (Preece papers) and Bodleian (MS. Marconi, Bristol Channel 1897 file): free catalogue enquiries for letters headed with the May 1897 address.

entries.title: A German spy reported on Marconi
entries.source: the project's working reading
entries.label: hypothesis
entries.cuts: The records found show Slaby as an invited guest who published his account; no intelligence file has been found.
entries.next: As above.

entries.title: A Post Office engineer named Williams puts up the Lavernock pole
entries.quote: Mr. Williams (of the engineering department, Cardiff)
entries.source: Evening Express, 15 May 1897, p.4
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: No first name, address or farm is given. A common surname; no record ties this man to Tŷ Mawr (Great House). No family relationship is assumed.
entries.next: BT Archives: free search request of the POST 59 establishment books for Cardiff engineering staff, 1897 (first name, grade, address).

entries.title: War Office, Admiralty and Post Office give Marconi facilities
entries.quote: Special facilities for making further experiments have been accorded the inventor by the War Office, the Admiralty, and the Postal Department
entries.source: Weekly Mail, 1 May 1897, p.4
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: Names the bodies, not people or places; nothing about lodgings or Llandough.
entries.next: BT Archives POST 30 (Marconi) catalogue enquiry, free.

entries.title: Kemp's diary of the trials
entries.quote: Lavernock pole "107 ft", Flat Holm "110 ft", apparatus left "at Penarth"
entries.source: George Kemp's diary (Bodleian MS. Marconi 89), extracts in G. R. M. Garratt
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: No mention of Great House Farm.
entries.next: Bodleian: free enquiry whether the full diary for 1-20 May 1897 names lodgings.

entries.title: Royal Engineers and a War Office observer at the trials
entries.quote: the War Office authorities ... have appointed an officer to watch the experiments carried out under the auspices of the G.P.O.
entries.source: Capt. W. P. Brett, R.E., lecture of 9 Dec 1897, Minutes of Proceedings of the Royal Artillery Institution vol. 25 (1898) p.111 ff.
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Royal Engineers at the trials, not logistics; nothing about where anyone stayed. Not yet in the evidence catalogue.
entries.next: none needed for the fact; the officer's name is in the RE records (free TNA catalogue search).

entries.title: Professor Slaby of Berlin at the trials, at the Kaiser's expense
entries.quote: The German Emperor had shown a marked interest in the invention and there had been present during the past week, and at the expense of the Emperor William, the learned Professor Slaby.
entries.source: South Wales Echo, 17 May 1897 (special edition), p.2
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: He attended openly as Preece's guest and the press named him; a 'spy' reading is a later interpretation.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Kemp: the first message went to the Kaiser through Slaby
entries.quote: This message was posted to the Kaiser by Professor Slaby.
entries.source: George Kemp's diary, 1930 fair copy, entry for 13 May 1897, quoted by G. R. M. Garratt (The Diary Junction, 2017)
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: The 1930 version was rewritten from the original, which brackets 10-14 May in one line.
entries.next: Bodleian: free enquiry for the original 1897 page.

entries.title: Annual inspection of the 2nd Glamorgan Volunteer Artillery at Lavernock
entries.quote: the annual inspection will take place at Lavernock on July 24, the inspecting officer being Colonel G. [initial unclear in the scan] Allen.
entries.source: Western Mail, 25 Mar 1897, p.8 (also Barry Dock News 21 May 1897 p.7)
entries.label: record
entries.kind: press (OCR text; obvious OCR slips corrected)
entries.cuts: After the trials; routine.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Preece's Lavernock–Flat Holm link handed to the War Office
entries.quote: Since March 1898 this system has been permanently established for signalling between Lavernock Point and the Flat Holm, and has been handed over to the War Office.
entries.source: J. J. Fahie, A History of Wireless Telegraphy (1899/1901)
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Preece's induction system, not Marconi's.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Slaby's own account: he took part, then built the German system for the Kaiser, army and navy
entries.quote: Quickly making up my mind, I traveled to England, where the Bureau of Telegraphs was undertaking experiments on a large scale. Mr. Preece ... in the most courteous and hospitable way, permitted me to take part in these ... on the morning of May 13, 1897, our party of five, cowering together in a big wooden case ... Having returned to my home, I went to work at once to repeat the experiments with my own instruments
entries.source: A. Slaby, 'The New Telegraphy', Century Magazine, April 1898, pp.867-874
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: He was invited and wrote openly; the article also names the German army balloon department and the navy as users afterwards, not before. MI5 did not exist until 1909, so no MI5 file of 1897 can exist.
entries.next: IET Archives: free catalogue enquiry for Preece–Slaby letters, 1897; TNA Discovery search of FO 64 (Germany) for Slaby, free.

entries.title: Proposed submarine minefield at Lower Penarth and Lavernock
entries.quote: Foreshores. Proposed submarine minefield at Lower Penarth and Lavernock.
entries.source: TNA MT 10/828/5, catalogue description
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: After the trials; the coast, not Llandough.
entries.next: Read at Kew (free).

entries.title: What Crichel Down was: land bought by the Air Ministry for a bombing range
entries.quote: the Air Ministry purchased this area of 725 acres of chalk down-land before the war for use as a bombing range. The land was not requisitioned. It was bought outright from three owners
entries.source: Sir Thomas Dugdale, HC Deb 20 July 1954 vol 530 cc1178-298
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: The Crichel Down case concerns land a military department bought; no Llandough land is known to have been bought by a military body.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: WGR monthly grazing let of the 5.30 a. Parcel B to John Williams
entries.quote: (monthly grazing tenancy, 8s a month, pasture only; plan coloured pink)
entries.source: Glamorgan Archives DBDT/123/7
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: A private letting (WGR), not a War Agricultural Executive Committee act.
entries.next: Glamorgan Archives: free catalogue enquiry for DSA/14/91 (1936 sale particulars) to see who held the land before 1939.

entries.title: The WAEC used Parcel B
entries.source: the project's working reading; a 2026 family letter to The National Archives puts it as the field BP obtained in 1969
entries.label: hypothesis
entries.cuts: No document found shows the WAEC in possession of Parcel B. Possession by a WAEC was returned (derequisitioned) to the person entitled, with no purchase, so no offer-back would follow.
entries.next: Defra FOI/EIR (pending); TNA MAF 48 / MAF 157-182 requisition files by subject (free catalogue enquiry).

entries.title: Glamorgan WAEC minutes, Cardiff District Committee
entries.quote: MAF 80/3934: Cardiff District Committee, 28 Sep 1939 - 30 Jan 1948 (also MAF 80/3855-3861 executive minutes; MAF 80/3887-3889 farms sub-committee; MAF 80/3943 index)
entries.source: TNA MAF 80, catalogue entries
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: County-wide minutes; parcel not identified until read.
entries.next: View MAF 80/3943 (index) and MAF 80/3934 at Kew, free.

entries.title: Penarth Head Fort taken over by American forces
entries.quote: During the Second World War the fort and house were taken over by the American Armed Forces.
entries.source: Alan Thorne, Place Names of Penarth (1997), p.13
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Penarth Head, not Llandough.
entries.next: WO 192 fort record book for Penarth (free at Kew).

entries.title: Llandough school damaged by enemy action
entries.quote: Llandough C. of E. School. The latter school has not been used since damaged by enemy action in 1941.
entries.source: Penarth UDC, Medical Officer of Health report for 1944
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Wartime damage in the parish; nothing about the farm or a military body.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: National Farm Survey forms and map for the parish
entries.quote: Parish No. 39 Parish: Penarth (MAF 32/1220/39); annotated OS map Glamorgan XLVII (MAF 73/58/47)
entries.source: TNA MAF 32/1220/39 and MAF 73/58/47, catalogue entries
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Not read. The survey form records owner, tenant, grading and any part occupied by a Service department.
entries.next: Defra FOI/EIR on wartime MAF farm records (already pending, due 17 Nov 2026); otherwise view at Kew (free).

entries.title: WAEC dissatisfaction; a farm manager appointed
entries.quote: During the war my father had difficulty in farming the land to the satisfaction of the War Agricultural Executive Committee, owing to his age and in 1944 it was arranged that my husband should give up his job and run the farm as Manager for my father.
entries.source: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement, c.1974
entries.label: testimony
entries.cuts: Supervision of how the farm was run, not possession or a taking.
entries.next: MAF 32/1220/39 grading (A/B/C) for the holding.

entries.title: Glamorgan WAEC writes about farm-worker housing sites
entries.quote: During the year a letter was received from the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee with regard to the provision of houses for the agricultural workers, together with a list of suggested sites
entries.source: Cardiff RDC, Medical Officer of Health report for 1946, pp.37-38
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Cardiff RDC area generally; no site named.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: Nearest documented parallel: requisitioned land at Swanbridge, Sully
entries.quote: Land at Swanbridge, Sully, Glamorgan: complaints by owner about actions by the Ministry of Agriculture... following de-requisitioning of the land, requisitioned in 1941 under the Defence Regulations 1939.
entries.source: TNA BD 24/102
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Not Cedwyn land.
entries.next: none needed

entries.title: "A Welsh case of Crichel Down" at the county planning committee
entries.quote: This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down … The Glamorgan County Council, Penarth Urban and Cardiff Rural Councils and Western Ground Rents have walked in and taken …
entries.source: Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958, p.7 (speaker named as Mrs M. D. Buckler; the site's testimony page identifies her as Mary (Nancy) Williams)
entries.label: testimony
entries.cuts: She named three councils and a private company, not a military body or the WAEC. The full page image is not held.
entries.next: Glamorgan Archives: GCC Planning Committee minutes of 19 Nov 1958 (issue #447); the full Western Mail page (issue #446).

entries.title: Leckwith exchange-of-land order, two days later
entries.quote: MAF 11/1022 (Leckwith exchange-of-land order, Cardiff RDC, 21 Nov 1958)
entries.source: TNA MAF 11/1022, catalogue entry
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: An agriculture ministry order, not a military one; parcel not identified.
entries.next: View MAF 11/1022 at Kew (free).

entries.title: Ministry of Defence FOI on 1988: neither confirm nor deny for Special Forces; otherwise not held
entries.quote: (s.23(5) neither confirm nor deny for the Special Forces parts; no information held for the rest; upheld at internal review)
entries.source: WhatDoTheyKnow FOI2026/09019 and FOI2026/09190
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: s.23(5) is the standard reply for any Special Forces question; it confirms nothing either way.
entries.next: none (internal review done).

entries.title: Glamorgan Archives and the Postal Museum: no records found
entries.quote: (Glamorgan Archives: holds no records of past Post Office employees; Postal Museum: Marconi-related files are held at BT Archives)
entries.source: family requests, catalogued
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Both point to BT Archives, which has not yet been asked for staff records (EV-0310 was about telephone and wayleave records).
entries.next: BT Archives staff-records search request (free).

entries.title: First World War: the War Agricultural Committee's Cardiff area sheets and plans for Llandough and Leckwith
entries.quote: With: reference number, map number, name of holding, tenant, owner, area, arable, 1916 and quota to be ploughed, as follows: (a) 123 Llandough, (b) 124 Leckwith ... (b) Llandough [K.123] Glamorgan 6 inch sheet XLVII on which the parish boundary is marked, with sheet attached with details of holdings, tenant, area and of fields ploughed attached
entries.source: Glamorgan Archives DSA/43/1/1/3 (sheets for most of the parishes) and DSA/43/1/1/5 (parish plans), catalogue descriptions; the Cardiff area (DSA/43/1, 1916) lists the parishes of Leckwith and Llandough
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: A First World War plough-quota survey of every holding in the area, not a taking or requisition. The Great House Farm row has not been read.
entries.next: Glamorgan Archives: view DSA/43/1/1/3 sheet (a) and plan DSA/43/1/1/5 (b) in the search room (free) and record the Great House Farm row as written.

entries.title: The Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee's own papers (Hubert Alexander, chairman)
entries.quote: The Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee in World War II ... Hubert Alexander Chairman (1 file, 2 bundles). Barry Sub District, Sep 1939-31 May 1940: Bundle for the Parishes Penarth, Lavernock, Sully, Barry, St. Andrews Major, Michaelston Le Pit. Giving details of properties, area, grassland, wheat proposed to be sown and correspondence.
entries.source: Glamorgan Archives DSA/43/3, with DSA/43/3/1 (minutes 1939-1944), DSA/43/3/3 (executive papers 1941-1945), DSA/43/3/4/1 (Farms Sub-committee 1940-1941) and DSA/43/3/6 (Barry Sub District), catalogue descriptions
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Not read. Llandough and Leckwith are not named in the catalogue's parish bundles (Penarth, Lavernock and Sully are). No catalogue entry found shows any Tŷ Mawr (Great House) land directed or requisitioned. The county minutes at Kew are MIL-025.
entries.next: Glamorgan Archives: view DSA/43/3/6 bundle 2 and DSA/43/3/4/1 (free) for any Great House Farm entry.

entries.title: Leckwith bombing decoy: "Leckwith Civil QL and SF" at Cwrt-yr-Ala
entries.quote: Leckwith Civil QL and SF ... ST 140739. Built on the lawns of the Cwrt Yr Ala estate of 800 acres in total.
entries.source: Ivor Jones, Wartime Bombing Decoys in Wales (2015), decoy list (full-text search of the scanned copy; page not noted)
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: Cwrt-yr-Ala, on the Leckwith side of the Ely valley, about 3 km west of St Dochdwy's Church, Llandough (grid references compared); not Tŷ Mawr (Great House) land and no link to the farm.
entries.next: TNA Discovery search (free) for the decoy site's file among the Air Ministry decoy records, for its dates of use.

entries.title: Decoy fires in Leckwith Woods drew bombs away from Cardiff
entries.quote: intended to be a major raid on Cardiff, fires were lit in Leckwith Woods on the other side of the Ely River and many bombs dropped harmlessly there
entries.source: Malcolm Pill, A Cardiff Family in the Forties (1999) (full-text search of the scanned copy; page not noted)
entries.label: testimony
entries.cuts: A memoir; the raid's date is not given in the passage read. Leckwith Woods, not Tŷ Mawr (Great House) land.
entries.next: Read the full page in the borrowable copy (free Internet Archive loan) for the raid's date; Glamorgan Archives catalogue search (free) for Cardiff ARP incident records of that night.

entries.title: Llandough and Leckwith War Memorial Institute (charity 213965)
entries.quote: THE HALL REPRESENTS A MEMORIAL HALL TO THOSE INHABITANTS OF THE AREA OF BENEFIT WHO DIED IN THE 1914-1918 WAR. ... Area of benefit: LLANDOUGH AND LECKWITH AND THE SURROUNDING NEIGHBOURHOOD
entries.source: Charity Commission register, charity 213965, governing document (Scheme of the Commissioners dated 6 February 2001)
entries.label: record
entries.cuts: A memorial to the parish's dead, not a military presence. The names on the hall's plaques have not been read; War Memorials Online memorial 254737 did not answer on 7 Nov 2026 (not checked).
entries.next: Read the plaque names on War Memorials Online 254737 or the IWM War Memorials Register (free); list them as written, with no family relationship assumed.
